extracted.intended_audience: critical care clinician-researchers and ICU outcomes researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Design and analysis guidance for a prospective observational/quality-improvement study of daily transition to delirium in a medical ICU, including measurement of sleep and sedation exposures and multivariable longitudinal modeling of transitions. Focus on how to define outcomes, measure exposures, select covariates, and perform regression accounting for repeated measures and interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcome: transition to delirium
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition to delirium defined as change from a ‘normal’ (non-delirious, non-comatose) state to delirious state within 24 hours, measured using twice-daily CAM-ICU assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform delirium assessments twice daily (approximately 8am and 8pm) with the CAM-ICU; include coma status (via RASS) to ensure transitions are from non-coma, non-delirious baseline. Use the transition within 24 hours as the primary outcome for regression models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use validated measurement instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use established, validated tools: CAM-ICU for delirium, RASS for sedation/coma, and the Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ) for perceived sleep quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer validated instruments (RCSQ validated vs polysomnography). When using subjective measures (RCSQ), be aware of their validation limits and potential biases compared to gold standards like PSG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived sleep exposure measurement via RCSQ
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure daily perceived sleep quality with the RCSQ: a validated 5-item 100 mm visual-analogue scale assessing depth, latency, efficiency, quality, and number of awakenings; the average score represents overall sleep quality. Include an optional item for perceived nighttime noise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect RCSQ each day describing the previous night's sleep. If patients cannot complete it (delirium, language barrier, inability to use writing instrument), have the nightshift nurse complete the RCSQ as proxy, but account for possible patient-nurse differences in analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling proxy-rated RCSQ and rater bias
rubrics_metrics.description: If patients are unable to self-report, nurses may complete the RCSQ; prior literature shows high patient-nurse agreement but nurses may overestimate sleep quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform sensitivity analyses adjusting for rater (patient vs nurse) and recognize nurse overestimation may bias associations toward the null.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure variable definitions for sedation
rubrics_metrics.description: Define sedation exposures separately for bolus and continuous infusion administration of benzodiazepines and opioids; consider combined variables when co-administration is common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track bolus and infusion administration for both benzodiazepines and opioids. If two exposures are almost always co-administered (e.g., 95% overlap), combine into a single variable (e.g., 'sedative infusion') to reflect clinical reality and reduce collinearity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criteria for transition analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Include patients with ≥1 night in the MICU and with delirium assessments both before and after a full night in the MICU; analyze only the first MICU admission per patient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrict analysis to patient-days where a transition could be observed (non-delirious/non-comatose before the night and assessed after). Use only first admissions to avoid correlated admissions across the same patient without explicit modeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency and timing of delirium/sedation assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess delirium and coma twice daily at approximately fixed times (e.g., 8am and 8pm) using CAM-ICU and RASS respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent timing improves the ability to define daily transitions. Record RASS to identify coma (RASS −4 or −5) and exclude coma states when defining transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical approach for repeated daily outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multivariable logistic regression with generalized estimating equations (GEE) to account for within-patient correlations of repeated daily outcome measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GEE accounts for clustering of repeated observations per patient in longitudinal daily transition models. Report both bivariable and multivariable ORs and CIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Markov modeling for transition analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate a patient's prior-day delirium status as a covariate (Markov model) to properly model transitions from one day to the next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include prior-day status to control for autocorrelation in daily states and to explicitly model transition probabilities rather than independent daily outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covariate selection to avoid overfitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Select covariates for multivariable models a priori if they have a bivariable association with the primary outcome at p ≤ 0.20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this liberal bivariable threshold to screen candidate covariates while limiting the number of variables in the multivariable model to reduce overfitting. Pre-specify selection rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and handling of multicollinearity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess multicollinearity using variance inflation factors (VIFs) and address problems by recategorizing or omitting less relevant collinear variables (or combining them when appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If VIFs indicate collinearity (or near-complete co-administration—as in 95% overlap), combine variables (example: benzodiazepine infusion + opioid infusion → 'sedative infusion') or remove one variable to stabilize estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess possible statistical interactions (e.g., between ventilator status and sedative infusions) by adding interaction terms to the multivariable model and include significant interactions in the final model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test clinically plausible interactions and retain them when statistically significant and clinically meaningful; interpret stratified effects if interaction present (e.g., effect of sedative infusion differs by mechanical ventilation status).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling continuous predictors appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm appropriate modeling of continuous variables by evaluating their linear association with the log odds of the outcome (e.g., use scatterplot with a LOWESS smoother).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the relationship is non-linear, consider transformation or categorization rather than forcing linearity; visually inspect LOWESS plots to guide modeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance threshold and inference
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a two-sided significance level of p < 0.05 to denote statistical significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report two-sided p-values and 95% confidence intervals; avoid over-interpretation of borderline p-values and consider clinical significance alongside statistical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary statistics and univariable testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize continuous variables with median and interquartile range and categorical variables with proportions; compare groups using Wilcoxon rank-sum for continuous and chi-square or Fisher's exact tests for categorical variables as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose non-parametric tests when distributions are skewed. Use appropriate tests based on expected cell counts (Fisher's exact when small expected counts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of results (ORs, CIs, bivariable and multivariable models)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present both bivariable and multivariable odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals and p-values for each covariate and exposure of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include tables that show bivariable associations and the adjusted multivariable model; explicitly report model covariates and interaction terms included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform sensitivity analyses to evaluate whether findings are robust to potential biases (e.g., adjusting for RCSQ rater, presence of concurrent QI interventions, or restricting to first transitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report whether results are materially changed in sensitivity analyses to strengthen causal inference and show result stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit discussion of limitations and generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss limitations including sample size/power, missing relevant covariates (illness severity, restraints, other deliriogenic meds), lack of dosing information, use of subjective sleep measures instead of PSG, and single-center setting impacting generalizability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge how each limitation could bias results (direction and magnitude where possible) and recommend future study designs (e.g., use PSG, larger multicenter cohorts) to address these gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical/regulatory consideration: QI vs research
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify whether the project is classified as quality improvement or research and obtain IRB review/waiver as appropriate; indicate whether consent was required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document IRB determination (e.g., IRB chair deemed the MICU-wide sleep promotion effort 'quality improvement' not requiring consent) so readers understand ethical oversight and patient consent context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical relevance/interpretation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret findings in the context of existing guidelines and clinical recommendations (e.g., minimize sedative exposure per practice guidelines and Choosing Wisely recommendations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate statistically significant associations (such as sedative infusions with delirium in ventilated patients) to actionable clinical recommendations and prior literature to inform practice changes.
